In this lesson you will learn how data is transferred between different areas within the 8086 microprocessor. These transfers include moving data between its internal registers or between an internal register and a storage location in memory.
INTRODUCTIONM
This data transfer is accomplished by instructions that the microprocessors interprets and executes............

While the 8086 microprocessor has a group of instructions that are provided for data transfer, in this lesson we will be primarily concerned with instructions that move, load, or store data via the MOV statement.t........................................................
The type of data transfer performed is controlled by an instruction contained in a code.

DISCUSSION
Each instruction contains one or more bytes of information in hexadecimal form.

The computer instruction is composed of two parts: an opcode and an operand. The opcode specifies what action is to be performed such as move, load, add, or subtract. With the 8086 processor, the opcode can be up to two bytes in length.ww

The operand is the second part of the computer instruction. The operand identifies the data that will be processed by the microprocessor under the control of the opcode......................................................................................................................................
Operands can be data, an addresses, or both. In the example below, the operands 1A & 1B are data which will be placed in the AX register by the opcode B8.

The particular type of data transfer instruction will determine if the operand is data or a memory address.ytes are determined to be data or addresses depending on the type of data transfer instruction.

The instruction B8, is an example of an instruction written in assembly language. The instruction is written using alphanumeric symbols instead of the 1's & 0's of the microprocessor's machine code...croprocessor to move data to the AX register (both the AL and the AH registers).

To further aid in the understanding of computer instructions, each opcode operation is assigned a unique one, two, or three-letter combination. This letter representation of the opcode is called a Mnemonic. For example, the mnemonic for the opcode B8 is shown below.::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::

This English statement is called a Pseudocode..

These operands may be part of the instruction, stored in one of the 8086's internal registers, or stored at an address in memory. The 8086 microprocessor uses several different addressing modes to access memory and allow for the transfer of data. We will be discussing three commonly used addressing modes in this lesson...erwar
Transfer instructions are divided into three categories.
The first addressing mode which allows the 8086 to transfer data is the immediate addressing mode instruction...et's look at the immediate data transfer instructions first..

Each type of immediate addressing mode instruction consists of an opcode in the first byte, followed by data in the second and possibly third byte.su utionEach type of immediate transfer instruction consists of an Opcode in the first byte followed by data in the second and/or third bytes.

With the immediate addressing mode, the operand appears in the instruction, is typically a constant, and can be either a byte or word of data.cThere is no byte for an address. The data is not in a memory location, the data is in the instruction.

Data can also be transferred directly from one register to another. Technically, this type of transfer is referred to as register addressing versus direct addressing because the CPU performs all operations internally.
